name: wellbeing-purpose-and-drive
description: Wellbeing, Purpose and Drive: two traditions of wellbeing, measurement problems, adaptation and the set point, money, the replication problem, what actually holds up, relationships, sleep, movement and the physical substrate, time and attention, self-determination theory, intrinsic motivation and rewards, goals, habits and behaviour change, willpower, flow, procrastination, how meaning and happiness come apart, sources of meaning, work, vocation and calling, adversity and growth, finitude, interventions, burnout, self-criticism and self-compassion, the limits of individual technique, and the industry critique. Research orientation, not clinical guidance.
